channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Durigan vê retomada da Lei da Reciprocidade como “provável”
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan said the government is likely to reinstate the Economic Reciprocity Law or issue a provisional measure if the U.S. imposes new tariffs on Brazilian goods, aiming to shield the national economy. He stressed that the decision requires consultation with President Lula and that impacts will be assessed cautiously before action. Durigan also expressed concern over the PEC for community health agents, warning that its approval without a funding source would undermine fiscal balance and could prompt the government to seek judicial review at the Supreme Federal Court.

item.title: Flávio vai ao Flow na quarta e lança plano "Brasil Por Elas" na quinta
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro plans to launch the 'Brazil For Her' plan during a social media live on Thursday night (July 16), featuring administrator Daniella Marques, who is being considered as his running mate. The day before (July 15), he will give an interview to the Flow podcast in São Paulo. The decision to unveil the full plan in a live broadcast sparked internal debate, with some allies favoring a gradual rollout in 'homeopathic doses'.

item.title: Flávio pediu suspensão de tarifaço e propôs negociar se vencer
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, urged the United States to suspend the planned tariff increase set for July 2026 and to open negotiations after the elections, arguing that imposing tariffs before the vote would allow the Lula government to frame the measure as U.S. electoral interference. He had previously sent a letter in June to Secretary of State Marco Rubio requesting the cancellation of the tariffs, claiming they would cause 'serious harm' to Brazilians and that only Lula desires their imposition.

item.title: Senado aprova em 1º turno PEC considerada pauta-bomba pela equipe econômica
item.description: The Senate approved in first turn a PEC establishing special retirement rules for community health agents and endemic disease combat workers, with a vote of 73 in favor and 1 against. The proposal, labeled a 'budget bomb' by Lula’s economic team, sets retirement at age 57 for women and 60 for men with 25 years of contributions, and could cost between R$30 billion and R$54 billion over ten years. A second-round vote remains pending.

item.title: TSE prepara portaria que define regras para big techs combaterem desinformação a 3 meses de eleições
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) is drafting a regulation that sets detailed rules for digital platforms with over 5 million active users in Brazil to submit compliance plans aimed at countering disinformation, improper AI use, and coordinated inauthentic behavior during the 2026 elections. Plans must be submitted by August 16, ten days before the official electoral campaign period begins, and include safeguards against chatbots issuing voting opinions or gender-based political violence, advertiser identity verification, and public transparency measures. The TSE will require monthly compliance reports from August to November and impose sanctions for non-compliance.

item.title: Diretor da Fundação FHC cita 'desconhecimento' ao reagir a fala de Janja sobre primeiras-damas: 'Não merece comentário'
item.description: The director of the FHC Foundation, Sergio Fausto, dismissed Janja's claim that she is Brazil's first first lady to work 'effectively' in government as a 'lack of historical knowledge', stating it 'does not deserve comment'. Janja had argued that no previous first lady had such a workload, citing her daily presence at the Planalto, meetings, agendas, and trips, while comparing her role to that of Ruth Cardoso, former first lady under Fernando Henrique Cardoso, and alleging class-based prejudice due to her modest background and public university education.

item.title: ANTT já aplicou este ano quase R$ 1 bilhão em multas por descumprimento do piso mínimo do frete
item.description: The ANTT issued R$ 932.4 million in fines for violations of the minimum freight floor in 2026 (through June), nearing R$ 1 billion, due to enhanced electronic monitoring. This marks a dramatic increase from 2018, when only R$ 69,000 in fines were issued. The Senate approved a provisional measure that toughens penalties, including fines up to R$ 1 million, registration suspension or cancellation, and extends liability to intermediaries and digital platforms.

item.title: Câmara acelera tramitação do projeto que derruba ampliação de área de preservação no Pantanal
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved urgency regime for the bill that would repeal the expansion of the Taiamã Ecological Station in the Pantanal, allowing direct floor vote. The bill, authored by Deputy Coronel Fernanda (PL-MT), accuses the Lula government of lacking dialogue in expanding the protected area by 50,000 hectares in March. The government states the move aims to protect biodiversity, water resources, and traditional communities.

item.title: Vídeo de Michelle tem mais que o dobro do engajamento da carta de Bolsonaro
item.description: A video posted by former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro on June 24 generated 132% more engagement on social media (X, Facebook, and Instagram) than an open letter from former President Jair Bolsonaro supporting his son Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential bid. In the video, Michelle claims Flávio disrespected and humiliated her during a phone call about the PL party’s slate in Ceará, accumulating 3.9 million interactions compared to the letter’s 1.68 million. The engagement surge reflects the deepening family rift within the Bolsonaro clan, which had been evident since December 2023.

item.title: Senado aprova em 1º turno PEC da aposentadoria especial para agentes de saúde, com impacto de R$ 30 bilhões
item.description: The Senate approved in first round a constitutional amendment (PEC) creating special retirement for health agents, allowing retirement at age 57 for women and 60 for men with 25 years of contributions, with a fiscal impact estimated at R$ 27 billion. The measure includes community health agents, endemic disease controllers, and indigenous health and sanitation agents, and guarantees parity and integrality — principles abolished in the public sector 23 years ago. Despite regular procedure, the government is considering taking the case to the STF due to fiscal impact, while criticizing the label 'budget bomb' and the delay in voting on the 6x1 workday reform.

item.title: 'Pauta-bomba': Senado aprova em 1º turno aposentadoria especial para agentes comunitários de saúde
item.description: The Senate approved in first round a constitutional amendment (PEC) granting special retirement for community health agents and endemic disease fighters, with minimum retirement age of 57 for women and 60 for men after 25 years of contributions. Dubbed a 'budget bomb' by the Lula government, the measure carries a projected fiscal impact of R$27 billion over ten years and has already passed the Chamber of Deputies, awaiting only the second Senate vote for promulgation. The PEC also extends benefits to indigenous health and sanitation agents and bans temporary or outsourced hiring except in public health emergencies.

item.title: Senado aprova a MP do Frete após acordo entre governo e oposição
item.description: The Senate approved the Freight MP after a government-opposition agreement, preventing its expiration on Thursday. The measure strengthens enforcement of the minimum freight rate for road cargo transport and now heads to President Lula for sanction. Key disagreements, including amnesty for post-2022 blockade fines and a R$ 5,000 minimum wage for drivers, were resolved via veto or adjustment.

item.title: Os bastidores da reunião de Nunes Marques com os institutos de pesquisas no TSE
item.description: TSE President Nunes Marques met with polling institutes to propose an 'Electoral Accuracy Seal' — a symbolic award for institutes whose polls most closely match election results. The gesture was deemed insufficient by representatives, who see it as a weak attempt to mend tensions caused by his earlier injunction suspending the AtlasIntel poll on Flávio Bolsonaro, a move widely viewed as excessive judicial interference in polling methodology.

item.title: PRTB anuncia Leonardo Avalanche como pré-candidato à Presidência
item.description: The PRTB announced Leonardo Avalanche as its pre-candidate for President in the 2026 elections, following the ineligibility of Pablo Marçal, who left the party and joined União Brasil. Avalanche, national president of PRTB since February 2024, presents his candidacy as a conservative alternative focused on tax reduction, economic growth, and strengthening popular participation. His background includes private sector work, judiciary-related activities, and organizing Marçal’s 2024 São Paulo mayoral campaign, though he is under judicial investigation for alleged fraud in an internal party election.

item.title: Senado aprova MP do Frete e enterra possível crise de Lula a menos de três meses da eleição
item.description: The Senate approved the MP changing the minimum freight floor rules, keeping the floor but removing the fixed 5,000 reais value as unconstitutional. The measure includes amnesty for fines against truckers for 2022 protests, a provision the Lula government plans to veto. Approval avoids a strike that could trigger a political crisis less than three months before the 2026 elections.

item.title: Eleições 2026: saiba os próximos passos para oficializar candidaturas
item.description: The 2026 electoral race is entering a decisive phase with party conventions scheduled from July 20 to August 5, when candidates for president, governor, senator, and federal, state, and district deputies will be officially nominated. Following the conventions, parties must submit official registration requests to the Electoral Justice by August 15, with the TSE reviewing presidential candidacies and TREs handling state and federal positions. Strict rules apply, including gender quotas (30%-70% per gender) and limits on candidacies per office, with non-compliance risking the rejection of entire slates.

item.title: TSE sugere selo para premiar institutos de pesquisas eleitorais
item.description: TSE President Minister Nunes Marques proposed the creation of a seal to award polling institutes that most accurately predict election results, aiming to incentivize quality and precision in public opinion surveys.

item.title: Papo Antagonista: Janja ataca ex-primeiras-damas: ‘nunca trabalharam efetivamente’
item.description: First Lady Janja criticized former Brazilian first ladies, stating that none had worked 'effectively' before her. She also expressed support for Michelle Bolsonaro and Senator Damares Alves, who have faced recent attacks. The remarks were made on the 'Papo Antagonista' program on Tuesday, the 14th.

item.title: Brasil TecPar e Allrede Telecom apresentam planos de expansão durante imersão no Centro-Oeste
item.description: Brasil TecPar and Allrede Telecom presented expansion plans during an immersion in the Center-West, visiting Brasília and Goiânia between July 7 and 10. The agenda included the Lidera Brasil 2026 event, which gathered around 150 participants in the federal capital to discuss growth strategies and present regional operation figures. The region’s infrastructure includes over 9,500 km of metropolitan networks, serving nearly 400,000 residential customers, more than 4,000 small businesses, approximately 2,200 large corporate accounts, and 140 wholesale providers, with services ranging from connectivity to edge computing and AI solutions, as regional director Gil Alves attributed results to the region’s dynamic economy.

item.title: Juíza condena deputado do PT por vídeo que retrata Tarcísio como o boneco Chucky
item.description: Judge Domitila Manssur of the São Paulo Regional Electoral Court (TRE-SP) ordered PT deputy Emídio de Souza to pay a 10,000-real fine for publishing an AI-generated video that associated Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) with the fictional character Chucky and scenes of explosions, vandalism, crime, and feminicide. The court ruled the content went beyond political satire by constructing a narrative that symbolically attributes responsibility for violence to the governor. While the defense claimed it was a caricature, the judge emphasized the illegality stems from linking the manipulated image to violent acts, not merely from using AI.

item.title: Lula compara próteses do SUS com “dentadura de Trump”
item.description: President Lula stated that dental prostheses provided by Brazil's SUS are superior to Donald Trump's denture, emphasizing the purchase of 880 vans for mobile dental clinics in remote areas. He highlighted the government's commitment to public health and access to services for vulnerable populations.

item.title: Aumento do eleitorado idoso pauta campanhas, mas abstenção é desafio
item.description: Brazil's elderly electorate reached 36.8 million in 2026, representing 23% of the total voting population and becoming a decisive segment for the October elections. Experts note this group prioritizes public health, pensions, social assistance, and cost of living, though their political orientation varies by income, religion, region, and other factors. Despite their growing importance, abstention among voters over 70 — whose vote is voluntary and without penalty — remains a challenge for campaigns.

item.title: Regra que impede Tarcísio de ser candidato deveria ser revista
item.description: The constitutional rule requiring officeholders to resign six months before elections to run for another office, though intended to prevent misuse of public resources, is criticized for being inconsistent, as it does not apply to those seeking re-election. This distortion excludes competitive candidates like Tarcísio de Freitas, who could run for president while remaining governor, thereby narrowing the field of viable contenders. The article suggests the next Congress will likely revisit this rule, as it limits the interests of those in power.

item.title: Valdemar diz que Flávio precisa se acertar com Michelle
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL, states that Flávio Bolsonaro must reconcile with Michelle Bolsonaro to unify the political group and secure Jair Bolsonaro's release, warning that without this agreement, the former president will remain imprisoned longer. He adds that if elected, Flávio would grant pardons to Jair Bolsonaro and those involved in the January 8 attacks, allowing the former president to resume party activities by late January. The remarks follow public disagreements between Michelle and Flávio over supporting Ciro Gomes in the Ceará gubernatorial race, which led Michelle to step down as head of PL Women.

item.title: Justiça manda penhorar pagamentos da Superbet a Romário por danos em mansão
item.description: The 10th Civil Court of Brasília ordered the seizure of future payments from Superbet and CazéTV to Senator Romário (PL-RJ) to settle a debt of R$ 865,000 stemming from property damage to a Lago Sul mansion between 2012 and 2016. The amount, updated with monetary correction, interest, and fees, originated from an initial R$ 268,000 ruling. This marks the second such asset freeze in under a week, following a R$ 32.4 million seizure order from Rio de Janeiro’s 4th Civil Court.

item.title: Lula defende parceria com empresários para disputar mercado externo
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) urged the government and business leaders to collaborate so Brazil can compete in foreign markets, advocating for multinational automakers to use Brazilian factories as export bases for Latin America instead of shipping directly from their headquarters. The remarks were made during a meeting with Anfavea, which projects 3 million vehicle registrations in 2026 — the highest since 2014. Lula noted his experience as both a union leader and president, stating it was easier to organize with foreign firms due to their historical union culture, and praised the automotive sector for its dynamic labor-management relations.

item.title: A condição para Carlos Portinho ser candidato do PL ao Senado pelo Rio
item.description: Carlos Portinho was chosen by Flávio Bolsonaro to run for Senate re-election in Rio de Janeiro, but the decision hinges on including Rogéria Bolsonaro on the ticket — either as his substitute or as a candidate for the second Senate seat. This condition aims to strengthen the Bolsonarist slate after Cláudio Castro’s disqualification and resolves the internal PL contest with Carlos Jordy. The outcome will shape the party’s reorganization in the state, weakened by Federal Police operations.

item.title: Saiba o que diziam regras da prisão de Lula e o que dizem as de Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes suspended for 90 days the visitation rights of Flávio Bolsonaro to his father, Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest, drawing comparisons to Lula’s 2018 imprisonment. While Lula, convicted in second instance by the Lava Jato operation, was allowed interviews, letters, and visits from public figures without restrictions on public dissemination, Bolsonaro was convicted of leading a coup attempt with final transit in julgado and faces stricter measures, including the suspension of visits. The legal differences between the cases — procedural stage, nature of charges, and court rulings — explain the distinct conditions of their incarceration.

item.title: 'É confundir ciência com bola de cristal', diz associação de institutos de pesquisa sobre 'selo' proposto pelo TSE
item.description: The Abep criticized the TSE's proposal to create the 'Electoral Accuracy Seal', arguing that equating polls with predictions is like confusing science with a crystal ball. The association warned the seal could incentivize opportunistic behavior, as institutes might adjust numbers to match consensus rather than uphold methodological rigor. Abep emphasized that poll quality should be judged by transparency, sampling, and scientific best practices — not by proximity to future election results.

item.title: Portaria do TSE sobre planos de conformidade abre metodologias de plataformas
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) is preparing to issue a regulation that implements Article 125-B of the electoral propaganda resolution, requiring digital platforms with over 5 million monthly active users in Brazil to develop compliance plans to prevent and mitigate risks to electoral integrity. The plans must detail preventive measures across ten duty categories, with public summaries and restricted TSE access to implementation evidence, shifting from a reactive to a preventive governance and transparency model.

item.title: Deputado do PT é multado em R$ 10 mil por vídeo de Tarcísio como boneco Chucky
item.description: State deputy Emídio de Souza (PT) was fined R$10,000 for publishing an AI-generated video on social media depicting Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) as the Chucky doll from the 'Child's Play' franchise. The penalty was imposed for improper use of image and dissemination of offensive content via artificial intelligence. The case highlights growing concerns over deepfakes and digital ethics in electoral campaigns.

item.title: PT de Goiás mantém pré-candidatura de Luis Cesar Bueno ao governo
item.description: The Goiás state directory of the Workers' Party (PT) decided to maintain the pre-candidacy of Luis Cesar Bueno for governor, defying President Lula's preference for federal deputy Adriana Accorsi. The party's convention to officially nominate candidates has been set for August 4 ahead of the October elections. According to a Real Time Big Data poll from July 9, Luis Cesar Bueno polls at only 5%, placing him fourth in the electoral race.

item.title: Zema diz que carta de Bolsonaro é ‘mais que normal’ e Caiado afirma que Flávio ‘explora’ o pai
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) criticized Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to ban Senator Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting his father, Jair Bolsonaro, under house arrest. Zema called the measure 'more than normal' and accused the STF of applying 'double standards', referencing Lula's 2018 case. Caiado said Flávio is 'exploiting' his father by using the letter for political gain.

item.title: Decisão de Moraes abre margem para Michelle Bolsonaro comandar jogo político no PL
item.description: The decision by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes to ban visits from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to former President Jair Bolsonaro opens space for Michelle Bolsonaro to play a more prominent role in the political maneuvering within the Liberal Party (PL). Although she has indicated she does not seek to engage in further internal conflicts, her influence in the party’s succession dynamics is expected to grow as other Bolsonaro family members are sidelined from active politics.

item.title: Nem a dentadura de Trump é igual à do SUS, diz Lula
item.description: President Lula joked that the SUS provides dentures made via 3D scanning and printing — something even Trump’s dentures don’t match. He made the comment during a meeting with Anfavea at the Palácio do Planalto, highlighting the purchase of 880 mobile dental vans. Lula also noted he has publicly criticized Trump 63 times over 3.5 years, while Trump has mentioned him only 11 times in 1.5 years.

item.title: Em derrota para o governo, Alcolumbre diz que quer votar dois turnos de pauta-bomba com impacto de R$ 30 bi nesta terça-feira
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre announced he will vote on both rounds of the PEC creating special retirement for health agents on Tuesday, with an estimated R$ 30 billion impact on public accounts, despite government opposition. The proposal, now in its fifth and final debate session, allows retirement at age 50 for women and 52 for men, with parity, integralidade, and active-employee adjustments. Despite attempts to soften the proposal, the government's economic team says it remains fiscally unsustainable.

item.title: Carlos Portinho será candidato ao Senado pelo Rio em vaga deixada por Cláudio Castro
item.description: Fluminense PL leadership confirmed that Senator Carlos Portinho will be the party's Senate candidate for Rio de Janeiro, replacing former Governor Cláudio Castro, who withdrew after being linked to investigations involving banker Daniel Vorcaro. The official announcement is expected from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the coming hours. Portinho defeated Deputy Carlos Jordy in the internal selection, benefiting from his incumbent senatorial mandate and support from numerous interior mayors.

item.title: Tábata busca Planalto para votar PL da Misoginia antes do recesso
item.description: Federal Deputy Tabata Amaral (PSB-SP), rapporteur of the bill criminalizing misogyny, met with Planalto officials to secure a vote before the parliamentary recess, despite resistance from Christian and right-wing blocs. The bill, which already had urgency approved, prescribes 2 to 5 years in prison and fines, with increased penalties for offenders with large digital audiences or economic motives. Tabata argues the bill targets harmful online conduct, not innocuous comments, and says House Speaker Hugo Motta committed to scheduling the vote.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro escolhe Carlos Portinho como candidato ao Senado pelo PL no Rio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) has chosen Senator Carlos Portinho as the party's Senate candidate for Rio de Janeiro, ending an internal contest with federal deputy Carlos Jordy. The decision was influenced by mayoral support and concerns over Jordy's limited ability to expand votes beyond the core bolsonarist base. The seat became vacant after Claudio Castro's ineligibility, and a second Senate race emerged following the arrest of Márcio Canella for illegal possession of a rifle.

item.title: Caiado sai em defesa de Damares após aliada de Michelle ser alvo de onda de ataques: 'Direita é maior que isso'
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado defended Senator Damares Alves after she faced misogynistic attacks and threats against her indigenous daughter, stating that the right must rise above such behavior. Caiado also intensified his criticism of Flávio Bolsonaro, claiming his campaign is sinking and that Lula treats him like 'a Christmas turkey'.

item.title: PL escala Carlos Portinho para disputa ao Senado no Rio
item.description: The PL has designated Senator Carlos Portinho as its Senate candidate for Rio de Janeiro, following the withdrawal of Cláudio Castro amid Federal Police investigations. The decision was made by Flávio Bolsonaro and Jair Bolsonaro. Portinho, who assumed office as a substitute in 2020, is seen as a consensus figure untainted by scandal, with appeal beyond the core bolsonarist base.

item.title: Vai à CCJ projeto que dificulta liberdade provisória para presos em flagrante
item.description: The Senate approved a bill that restricts provisional liberty for individuals arrested in flagrante in serious cases such as recidivism, militia participation, illegal possession of restricted firearms, heinous crimes, and others, requiring judges to justify any release. Originally proposed by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the bill was expanded by rapporteur Marcio Bittar to include more offenses while still allowing judges to grant provisional liberty with clear reasoning. The bill now proceeds to the Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ).

item.title: Crusoé: Lula autoriza educação política na escola: ideologização?
item.description: President Lula signed a bill making political education and citizenship rights a mandatory component of basic education, integrated into the study of social and political reality. The measure aims to foster critical and engaged citizenship, though it has sparked debate over potential ideological indoctrination in schools.

item.title: Correia diz que Flávio usou visita a Bolsonaro como “gabinete político”
item.description: Federal Deputy Rogério Correia (PT-MG) criticized the 90-day ban imposed by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes on Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) from visiting former President Jair Bolsonaro, claiming the visits were being used as a 'political cabinet'. Correia argued the measure prevents Flávio from leveraging his proximity to the ex-president for political articulation and institutional influence.

item.title: Janones: ‘A meta não é mais eleger Lula, mas dizimar, exterminar o bolsonarismo’
item.description: Federal deputy André Janones (Rede-MG) stated that the goal for 2026 should no longer be merely re-electing Lula, but the 'complete extermination of bolsonarism'. He argues that only a landslide Lula victory in October can definitively end bolsonarism's influence, warning that a narrow win would leave the movement alive for at least four more years. Janones declared he is ready to 'kill or die' for the cause, amid Lula's lead in polls and Flávio Bolsonaro's struggles to regain electoral support.

item.title: Deputadas cobram aprovação de projeto que criminaliza misoginia antes do recesso na Câmara
item.description: The female caucus in Brazil's Chamber of Deputies urged the urgent approval of a bill equating misogyny with racism before the parliamentary recess began on Saturday. Although Chamber President Hugo Motta had committed to voting on the proposal, the vote was postponed due to opposition from religious deputies who fear misinterpretation and the criminalization of biblical texts. Female lawmakers stressed the bill does not target religion or free expression but seeks to criminalize violence against women in any setting.

item.title: Renan Santos compara Janja à Maria Antonieta
item.description: Renan Santos, a pre-candidate for presidency from the Missão party, criticized First Lady Rosângela da Silva (Janja) for her remarks on international travel expenses, comparing her attitude to that of Marie Antoinette. He accused her of being out of touch with ordinary Brazilians and pledged to increase transparency in presidential spending. The video was posted on his social media and sparked widespread discussion.

item.title: Nova lei inclui educação política e direitos da cidadania no currículo do ensino básico
item.description: President Lula signed Law 15.468/26, which mandates political education and citizenship rights as compulsory content in the national basic education curriculum. The law approves Bill 1108/15, proposed by licensed Deputy Renata Abreu (Pode-SP), aiming to prepare students to understand how Parliament works and the Brazilian Constitution.

item.title: Empresas de pesquisa criticam proposta do TSE de criar ‘selo de qualidade’ para levantamentos
item.description: TSE President Minister Kassio Nunes Marques' proposal to create an 'Electoral Accuracy Seal' awarding polling institutes whose surveys closest match official election results has drawn criticism from major research firms. They argue the initiative mistakenly treats voter intention polls as predictions, ignoring that opinions can shift between interviews and voting. The proposal followed the suspension of an AtlasIntel poll showing a six-point drop for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, which firms labeled censorship, and was seen as counterproductive due to perceived lack of understanding of polling methodology by the minister.

item.title: Dino chama terceirização de emendas de ‘esdrúxula’ e critica cota a ex-parlamentares
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino stated that only sitting congressmembers can propose and deliberate on parliamentary amendments, declaring 'outsourcing' of amendments illegal. He criticized informal budgetary centers and the transfer of budget control to non-parliamentarians, calling it a constitutional vice, and ordered asset freezes totaling R$125 million against Valdemar Costa Neto and Eduardo Cunha for allegedly indicating amendments without authority.
